feature_title: oem_wh Fabric Warehouse (DDL-only SQL-queryable layer over gold)
rationale: A Fabric Warehouse item that nothing has ever read. It was never a deliberate design choice: it entered the repo in commit 6a27b25 (2025-08-18), an auto-generated Fabric git-sync commit that captured it alongside oem_lh at workspace creation, before the task system existed. Measured live on 2026-08-10 before removal: the semantic model OEMInsightBI_v2 has exactly one source expression, 'DirectLake - oem_lh', resolving to AzureStorage.DataLake(.../488fb9f8-e635-4683-90c4-ba4fee9dfadb) - the LAKEHOUSE guid - with all 14 tables at mode: directLake; the warehouse guid b1cb7506 and the literal 'oem_wh' appear ZERO times across all 20 semantic-model parts. The live orchestrator pipeline (10 activities) references it zero times. No notebook writes to it (no JDBC, no synapsesql, no T-SQL sink). DEC-012 had already recorded, after Erik ran index DDL against it live on 2026-08-03, that there is 'no documented SQL-endpoint consumer of oem_wh'. Worse than unused, it was actively misleading for a portfolio project: a TDS query of sys.objects returned 8 tables, ZERO views and ZERO stored procedures - refuting the spec's claim of 4 views plus usp_merge_fact_procurement and usp_refresh_quality_metrics - and its data was a frozen 2026-01-16 snapshot diverging from the live lakehouse in both directions (fact_epi_score 206 vs 12196; fact_supply_share 58542 vs 3463). Anyone opening the warehouse to sanity-check the report would have got numbers contradicting it. Meanwhile deploy-fabric.yml listed 'Warehouse' in item_type_in_scope, so CI redeployed the empty DDL on every merge. Retirement mechanism chosen by Erik 2026-08-10, following the bronze-azuresqldb2table-dataflow precedent.
restore_notes:
READ THIS BEFORE RESTORING.

0. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY GET BACK IS EIGHT EMPTY TABLES. The snapshot is DDL-only: 8 CREATE TABLE statements with every column nullable, no keys, no constraints, no indexes, and zero DML anywhere in the folder. There has NEVER been an automated load path into this warehouse - no pipeline activity, no notebook write, no Copy Job. The rows that were in it (as of 2026-01-16) arrived by an ad-hoc load that is not reproducible from this repo. Restoring the folder gives you schema, not data.

1. COMMIT PIN. commit_sha is the last commit where the warehouse was live in main (HEAD immediately before the retirement commit), per rules/feature-retirement.md Step 2.

2. THE SPEC IS NOT A RESTORE CHECKLIST - IT DESCRIBES OBJECTS THAT NEVER EXISTED. spec_v1.md lines ~1207-1219 list 4 views (v_procurement_summary, v_supply_concentration_risk, v_supplier_sustainability_scorecard, v_data_quality_overview) and 2 stored procedures (usp_merge_fact_procurement, usp_refresh_quality_metrics) as living 'in oem_wh', and line ~1608 calls that layer 'already implemented'. A live TDS query of sys.objects WHERE is_ms_shipped=0 on 2026-08-10 returned 8 USER_TABLEs and NOTHING ELSE - zero views, zero procedures, all 8 tables with modify_date == create_date == 2026-01-16 08:14. Those objects were specified and never built. Three of the v_* names DO exist, but as Spark-catalog views created inside silver_to_gold.Notebook over the lakehouse (task-038_2 established they are 'invisible to the SQL endpoint'). Do not restore expecting to find them.

3. RESTORING DOES NOT CHANGE THE SERVING PATH. The semantic model reads the lakehouse via DirectLake-on-OneLake and never touched this warehouse. If your goal is to put a warehouse in the serving path, that is new design work (a gold -> warehouse sync plus repointing the model), not a restore.

4. DEPLOY SCOPE. .github/workflows/deploy-fabric.yml had 'Warehouse' removed from item_type_in_scope at retirement. Re-add it or fabric-cicd will not publish the restored DDL.

5. TWO RELATED SQL FILES ARE NOT IN THIS SNAPSHOT AND ARE NOT DEPLOYABLE DDL. fabric/sql/warehouse_indexes.sql is a DEC-012 finding document (100% comments; CREATE INDEX is rejected by Fabric DW with Msg 22424) and stays in tree. fabric/create_quality_views.sql carries the instruction 'Run this script in the oem_wh warehouse after gold layer loads' - it was never actually run (measured: zero views), and its target was updated at retirement. Neither is part of a restore.

6. xmla.json IS NOT YOUR SEMANTIC MODEL. It is the auto-generated DEFAULT semantic model every Warehouse item carries, still holding unfilled template placeholders ({{Dataset_Name}}, {{Partition_Name}}, {{TDS_Endpoint}}). The real Power BI model is fabric/OEMInsightBI_v2.SemanticModel/. Do not conflate them.

7. DO NOT CONFUSE THREE THINGS NAMED SIMILARLY. (a) oem_lh the Lakehouse (488fb9f8-...), where all medallion Delta tables live. (b) oem_lh's SQL analytics endpoint (f9bb3de4-...), auto-created, reports as type Warehouse in some APIs, read-only, still live. (c) oem_wh, THIS item (b1cb7506-...), a standalone Warehouse. Only (c) was retired. Note both (b) and (c) share the same TDS host 2binpjytvaeevef26xkmilpx4e-nxgojgodn2tutlwzw2nqjkl2ve.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com and are distinguished only by database name.

8. SPEC MARKERS TO REVERT. spec_v1.md carries Retired (2026-08-10) markers added via /iterate per DEC-016 - do NOT edit the spec inline. Locations at retirement: ~48 (Secondary Purpose / hybrid Lakehouse+Warehouse claim), ~80 (Fabric Artifacts list), ~682 (Orchestration planned warehouse sync), ~1191-1225 (Warehouse Configuration), ~1608 (Remaining Work item 2).

9. UNMARKED MIRROR DOCS. README.md, docs/architecture/fabric_workspace.md, docs/architecture/medallion_architecture.md, docs/architecture/orchestration.md, docs/architecture/semantic_model.md, docs/architecture/fabric-artifacts-inventory.md, docs/portfolio/CASE_STUDY.md, docs/standards/naming_standards.md, docs/standards/sql_standards.md and docs/glossary.md all mention it. They take no retirement marker and were updated at retirement - check them on restore.

10. RELATED DECISION. DEC-012 (decision-012-warehouse-index-retire.md, 2026-08-03) retired warehouse-index work on the finding that nothing queries oem_wh. It was not the driving decision for THIS retirement, but it is the strongest prior evidence and should be re-read before any restore.
